name: Movie Recap Chop Delete Flip Speed Transform
use_when: A movie recap paragraph has a verified source scene range that is much longer than the narration.
The edit needs transformed visuals rather than a continuous movie excerpt.
The source scene needs to be compressed into a fast short-form recap rhythm.
The project uses muted source visuals under narration.
avoid_when: The shot contains readable text, maps, UI, or direction-critical action that would become confusing when mirrored.
The scene requires a continuous emotional performance or clear geography that would be damaged by rapid deletion.
The user asks for a slow cinematic recap rather than short-form transformed fragments.

timeline_pattern.pattern: verified_scene_range -> mute_source_audio -> chop_2_to_3s_fragments -> delete_alternate_fragments -> mirror_alternate_retained_fragments -> speed_fit_to_voiceover -> render_spot_check
timeline_pattern.chunk_rule: Use roughly 2-3 second chunks as the default starting point. Adjust chunk length only for action readability, scene clarity, or narration timing.
timeline_pattern.deletion_rule: After chopping, remove alternating chunks to compress the source and avoid a continuous scene run.
timeline_pattern.flip_rule: Mirror alternating retained chunks, not every chunk. Skip mirroring when it hurts readability or continuity.
timeline_pattern.speed_rule: Use speed changes only to fit narration or preserve a key visual beat. Do not stretch raw footage by dragging handles when speed adjustment is the intended transform.

motion.rule: The transform pattern itself creates motion variety. Add zooms, shakes, or overlays only when they serve the recap beat.
motion.avoid: Stacking extra effects on top of fast fragments until the scene becomes unreadable.

sound.rule: Keep narration dominant. Optional music or SFX stays low and follows visible events.
sound.avoid: Using the movie's original soundtrack as the main sound bed.

captions.rule: Captions should be timed to narration and placed away from the scene's action center.
captions.avoid: Caption placement that hides the key event in a short fragment.

color.rule: Apply a consistent light grade after fragment selection so the retained shots feel like one recap unit.

implementation.ffmpeg: Generate fragment rows from the verified source range. Drop alternating rows, add hflip on selected retained rows, apply setpts for optional speed changes, mute source audio, and mix narration as primary audio.
implementation.remotion: Create an array of visual fragments with start, end, keep, mirror, playbackRate, and narrationWindow fields. Render from the array so the transform is auditable.
implementation.blender: Use the VSE only for special manual versions; keep the same fragment metadata in project notes.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Blade the selected scene every 2-3 seconds, delete every other clip, mirror alternating retained clips, then adjust speed for timing against the voiceover.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use markers or an automated EDL to cut 2-3 second subclips, remove alternating clips, apply Horizontal Flip to selected retained clips, and use Speed/Duration for timing.

common_mistakes: Applying the three-second chop before finding the correct scene.
Keeping a long unbroken movie run because it looks good.
Mirroring shots with text, asymmetric story details, or direction-critical movement.
Changing speed so much that action becomes unreadable.
Forgetting to recheck scene/narration alignment after deletion and speed changes.
Applying vertical blur/canvas treatment before the chop pattern is locked, causing inconsistent fragments.
qc: Is there any long continuous source run that should have been chopped?
Do retained fragments still match the paragraph narration?
Are mirrored fragments free of readable text or confusing direction changes?
Do speed changes preserve action readability?
Does the final paragraph unit end near the voiceover end without dead tail or cut-off narration?
Has a rendered contact sheet been reviewed after the transform?
